narrative.overview:
Mainframe is a native Mac work surface for someone running four to six coding agents at once. The workbench steps back so the work leads: grey ground, white sheets, hairlines a single pixel thin, and a system font in a few weights. Nothing in the chrome asks for attention unless an agent needs the user, something is running, or an action is ready. When several sessions are busy, the window should still read as quiet, scannable status.

The layout is the category standard that users of the Claude desktop app, Codex and Antigravity already know: a title bar with tabs, a session list on the left, a centred reading column with the composer under it, and optional panels on the right. Distinction comes from craft, not from a themed look. Columns line up from the title bar down, one 28 px row pitch runs through every list, each shortcut has a visible control, and narrowing the window never drops a control. Bold themed directions were explored and rejected; consumer-chat softness was rejected too.

Density is moderate and keyboard-first. Body text is 13 px, the transcript 14 px, and controls are 24–32 px. Colour is a signal, never decoration: blue for action, focus and live work, amber and red only when a state earns them, and provider brand colours only as small dots. Light and dark are equal citizens: every colour token has a `-dark` twin, and the dark theme compensates contrast instead of simply inverting.

This file is the approved target for the window revamp (sidebar, title bar, transcript, composer, session panel, workspace). The decision log is `~/Documents/Mainframe/design-council/2026-11-23-composer-canon/DECISIONS.md`, and the rendered states are the `Proposal-Redesign-*` boards on the "Mainframe App" canvas Proposals page. Settings, automations, tasks and mobile adopt the system later.
keyCharacteristics: Grey ground, white sheets and cards, one-pixel hairlines; depth by tone first, shadow second.
The system font stack only, in three weights (400, 500, 600) and sizes from 11.5 to 15 px.
One 28 px row pitch in the sidebar, session panel, activity strip, menus and toolbar.
Blue only where something can act or is acting; amber and red only for earned states.
Columns aligned from the title bar down; nothing disappears at narrow widths.
Status outranks settings: what the agent is doing is always the loudest thing on screen.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Blue appears only where something can act or is acting: focus, a ready Send, the caret, live work, the plan status. It is never a background wash, a resting border or decoration.

rules.name: The State-Earned Colour Rule
rules.body: Amber, rose and red appear only when a state earns them: amber for needs you, Auto and Unattended permissions and context at 80 %; rose for failed work; red for context at 95 %. A screen where every session is idle is entirely neutral apart from provider dots.

rules.name: The Provider Dot Rule
rules.body: Provider brand colours appear only as small dots beside a name. They never tint text, fills or borders.

rules.name: The Native Stack Rule
rules.body: Use the system font stack and the system monospace only. No webfonts, no display sizes above 15 px, and weights only 400, 500 and 600.

rules.name: The Mono Means Machine Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks strings the machine owns: code, commands, branches, paths, file names and rule patterns. UI labels such as "Worktree" or "from main" stay in the UI face.

rules.name: The Steady Number Rule
rules.body: Numbers that change in place (context percent, elapsed time, change counts, sub-agent counts, usage) use tabular figures, so nothing shifts as they update.

rules.name: The Aligned Seams Rule
rules.body: Every vertical edge in the title bar continues an edge below it. A separator that doesn't sit above a column edge is a bug.

rules.name: The 28 Pitch Rule
rules.body: Lists and toolbars use one 28 px row pitch. A new list row that is 30 or 32 px tall needs a reason (tabs and queued messages are 32 px because they hold a close or edit control).

rules.name: The Nothing Disappears Rule
rules.body: Narrowing merges, shortens or iconifies a control, and never removes one. Every shortened control keeps its full meaning in its tooltip and accessible name, and the context ring and permission status stay visible at every width.

rules.name: The Two-Lift Rule
rules.body: The composer card lifts slightly and floating surfaces lift clearly. Nothing else casts a shadow, and no resting border is thicker than 1 px.

rules.name: The Halo Means Waiting Rule
rules.body: A translucent ring around a card means it is waiting for the user: a pending gate. The focused composer has a solid line, not a ring. Never use it for emphasis.

rules.name: The One Slot Rule
rules.body: The composer's bottom-right slot holds the action that matters now: Send, Stop or Stopping. Only the Queue split may sit beside Stop, and only while the agent runs with text typed.

rules.name: The No-Confirm Stop Rule
rules.body: Stopping is always one click or one keystroke (⌘.), in the composer and in the activity strip. The result is reported afterwards (a toast or a transcript line), never asked for before.

rules.name: The Exclusive Environment Rule
rules.body: Local, worktree and temporary are one choice with one answer. Temporary never has a branch or worktree, and the UI shows this by locking the control, not hiding it.

dos: Do use the 28 px row pitch for every new list, and align new title bar elements to the column edges below them.
Do put blue text in Blue Ink (`accent-ink`) and blue fills behind white text in Deep Blue Fill (`accent-fill`); System Blue (`accent`) is for the ready Send, the caret and tints.
Do keep the focus line a solid 2 px Focus Blue (2 px off a control, on a field's own edge), at 3:1 or better against the ground, card and hairline.
Do show status in the right slot of a row (spinner, "needs you", count) and keep the project letter in the leading slot.
Do use tabular figures for every number that changes in place.
Do design every surface in light and dark together, using the `-dark` twin of each token.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 (`meta` is the lowest text colour), targets at 24 px or more, and toolbar targets at 28 px.
Do give every shortened or icon-only control a tooltip and accessible name that carry its full meaning and shortcut.
donts: Don't use webfonts, sizes above 15 px, uppercase labels or weights other than 400, 500 and 600.
Don't use blue, amber or red as decoration, a background wash or a resting border.
Don't tint text, fills or borders with a provider colour; it is a dot only.
Don't add shadows beyond the card lift and the float shadow, or any resting border thicker than 1 px.
Don't wrap the composer in a frame or a different-grey box; strips tuck under the card.
Don't hide a control at narrow widths; merge, shorten or iconify it.
Don't confirm Stop; the one confirmation in the composer is turning on Unattended, once per session.
Don't use `faint` for text, draw a scrollbar track, or let a native scrollbar take width; scrollbars are overlay thumbs.
